note.question: Can a transparent, revisable matching process allocate scarce seats reliably when participants have private preferences and may not understand or play the benchmark mechanisms' equilibrium strategies?
note.overview: Students with private preferences repeatedly choose or revise college applications in an extensive-form matching game, observe rivals' latest choices, and act under common knowledge of rationality. The paper characterizes outcomes under every rationalizable strategy profile and compares them with Bayesian-Nash and dominant-strategy benchmarks.

models.method: Theoretically, we prove that efficient and stable matching occurs with an arbitrarily high probability, assuming sufficient revision opportunities and rationality.

methodEvidence.section: A Dynamic Matching Mechanism for College Admissions: Theory and Experiment

sources.quote: The mechanism selects a matching as a function of the accumulated actions from each student. • A dynamic mechanism is Pareto efficient (stable) relative to the true preference profile if the selected matching is always Pareto efficient (stable) when all players play the myopic best responding strategy.

components.label: Objective and constraints
components.explanation: At every recognition opportunity, a myopic best responder chooses the most-preferred college whose seat is not currently occupied by a higher-priority student; expected-utility rationality determines the broader set of rationalizable dynamic strategies.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Before a public terminal time, each student's independent Poisson clock generates recognition opportunities. At each recognition, the student observes every other student's latest college choice and may apply, keep the current choice, or switch. At the closing time, the mechanism mechanically assigns each college's seats to its highest-priority applicants up to capacity; the experiment compares this process with one-shot DA and Boston reports. Students move only when recognized but may revise repeatedly before a hard close.

components.label: Rationalizable-strategy outcome of the IM Dynamic extensive-form matching game
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Rationalizable-strategy outcome of the IM Dynamic extensive-form matching game. Theorem 1 states that for sufficiently large λ, the stable and efficient matching occurs with arbitrarily high probability under every rationalizable strategy profile. Static comparisons use truthful/dominant-strategy and Bayesian-Nash benchmarks for DA and Boston.
